name: Flinders Street Station
desc: Melbourne's Edwardian-Baroque railway landmark, its yellow facade, green dome and row of clocks a beloved city meeting point.

name: Parliament House, Canberra
desc: Set into Capital Hill with a grassed roof the public can walk over, the national parliament is topped by an 81-metre stainless-steel flag mast.

name: Royal Exhibition Building
desc: A grand dome-crowned pavilion built for the 1880 International Exhibition and Australia's first UNESCO World Heritage-listed building, set in the Carlton Gardens.

name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
desc: The world's largest steel-arch bridge when built, its granite-clad pylons and single span - the 'Coathanger' - remain a defining emblem of Sydney.

name: Sydney Opera House
desc: Utzon's sail-shell vaults over Sydney Harbour are a 20th-century architectural icon and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Museum of Old and New Art (MONA)
wiki: Museum of Old and New Art
desc: David Walsh's provocative private museum is carved largely underground into Triassic sandstone cliffs on the Berriedale peninsula; its subterranean galleries mean free-licensed exterior photos are scarce.

name: One Central Park
desc: A residential tower wrapped in Patrick Blanc's living vertical gardens, with a cantilevered heliostat that reflects sunlight down into the plaza below.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
desc: Niemeyer's hyperboloid crown of 16 sweeping concrete columns is one of modernism's most recognisable churches, its interior lit through a stained-glass ceiling.

name: National Congress of Brazil
desc: The centrepiece of Niemeyer's planned capital pairs twin office towers with a dome and an upturned bowl housing the two legislative chambers.

name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
desc: A saucer-shaped gallery poised on a single slender stem above Guanabara Bay, reached by a curving red ramp, and among Niemeyer's most photographed late works.

name: SESC Pompéia
desc: Lina Bo Bardi turned a former drum factory into a cultural and sports centre, adding raw béton-brut towers with irregular cave-like window openings linked by aerial walkways.

name: São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP)
desc: Lina Bo Bardi suspended the museum's glass gallery box from four red concrete beams, freeing a vast public plaza beneath it on Avenida Paulista.

name: Museum of Tomorrow
desc: Calatrava's science museum reaches out over the water on a revitalised pier at Praça Mauá, its skeletal solar canopies a symbol of Rio's redeveloped port district.

name: Sesc 24 de Maio
desc: A Pritzker-winner's vertical leisure centre in a converted downtown department store, crowned by a much-loved rooftop swimming pool high above the city streets.

name: CN Tower
desc: At 553 metres it was the world's tallest free-standing structure for over three decades and remains Toronto's defining landmark. Its tapering concrete shaft carries a seven-storey SkyPod and glass-floored observation decks.

name: Canadian Museum of History
desc: Douglas Cardinal's flowing, curvilinear limestone forms evoke the glacier-carved Canadian landscape along the Ottawa River. It is Canada's most-visited museum and a landmark of organic architecture.

name: Habitat 67
desc: Built for Expo 67 from stacked prefabricated concrete modules, this experimental housing complex reimagined dense urban living with private terraces for every unit. It launched Moshe Safdie's career and remains a Brutalist landmark.

name: National Gallery of Canada
desc: Moshe Safdie's glass-and-granite gallery crowns a bluff overlooking the Ottawa River, its faceted glass towers echoing the Gothic spires of the nearby Parliament. The pink-granite pavilions house Canada's national art collection.

name: Notre-Dame Basilica
desc: An early and influential example of Gothic Revival architecture in Canada, with twin stone towers rising over Place d'Armes. Its deep-blue, star-studded vaulted interior is among the most celebrated in North America.

name: Absolute World Towers
desc: Nicknamed the 'Marilyn Monroe' towers for their sinuous curves, these twin residential highrises rotate continuously up their height. They were the first major North American project by China's MAD Architects.

name: Aga Khan Museum
desc: Pritzker laureate Fumihiko Maki clad this museum of Islamic art in white Brazilian granite set around a light-filled courtyard and reflecting pools. It is North America's first museum dedicated to Islamic arts and Muslim cultures.

name: Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest)
architect: Herzog & de Meuron with Ai Weiwei and Arup
desc: The main stadium of the 2008 and 2022 Olympics, whose interlacing steel lattice earned it the nickname 'the Bird's Nest' and made it a global symbol of contemporary China.

name: CCTV Headquarters
architect: OMA - Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren
desc: A radical continuous loop of two leaning towers joined by a cantilevered overhang, rethinking the skyscraper as a folded three-dimensional circuit.

name: Forbidden City
architect: Imperial court architects (chief designer Kuai Xiang)
desc: The vast Ming and Qing imperial palace complex at the heart of Beijing, the world's largest surviving wooden palace ensemble and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
wiki: National Centre for the Performing Arts (China)
desc: Nicknamed 'The Giant Egg', this titanium-and-glass dome floating on an artificial lake next to Tiananmen Square is one of Beijing's boldest modern landmarks.

name: Temple of Heaven
desc: A masterpiece of Ming religious architecture where emperors prayed for good harvests; its circular Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is built entirely without nails.

name: Beijing Daxing International Airport
architect: Zaha Hadid Architects with ADP Ingenierie
desc: The world's largest single-terminal airport, a radial starfish-shaped hub whose flowing steel roof funnels passengers from a central court to six splayed piers.

name: Harbin Opera House
desc: A sculptural, snow-white cultural landmark whose sweeping curves echo the wetlands and ice of northern China, widely praised as one of the decade's finest concert halls.

name: Shanghai Tower
desc: China's tallest building at 632 m, its twisting, tapering double-skin facade spirals 120 degrees to cut wind loads, crowning the Lujiazui skyline.

name: ARoS Aarhus Art Museum
architect: Schmidt Hammer Lassen (Your Rainbow Panorama by Olafur Eliasson)
desc: A cubic brick art museum crowned by Olafur Eliasson's Your Rainbow Panorama, a 150-metre circular walkway of coloured glass offering a spectrum-tinted view over the city. It is one of Scandinavia's largest art museums.

name: Bagsvaerd Church
desc: Behind a modest prefabricated concrete-and-glass shell, Jorn Utzon hid a luminous nave roofed by billowing cast-concrete clouds. It is regarded as a masterwork of critical regionalism, uniting industrial modernism with sacred light.

name: Copenhagen Opera House
desc: One of the world's most costly opera houses, its vast flat cantilevered roof floats over a glowing maple-clad auditorium on the Holmen waterfront. It sits on the harbour axis directly opposite the royal Amalienborg Palace.

name: Grundtvig's Church
architect: Peder Vilhelm Jensen-Klint (completed by Kaare Klint)
desc: A towering expressionist church built entirely of six million yellow bricks, its stepped west front rising like a colossal cathedral organ. It is the foremost example of Expressionist church architecture and a Danish national landmark.

name: 8 House (8 Tallet)
desc: A figure-of-eight mixed-use block whose sloping green roofs and continuous ramp let you cycle from street level to the tenth floor. BIG's 'three-dimensional neighbourhood' won the 2011 Scandinavian Green Roof Award.

name: CopenHill (Amager Bakke)
desc: A clean waste-to-energy plant doubling as public infrastructure, its sloping roof forming a year-round dry ski slope, hiking trail and the world's tallest climbing wall. It won the 2021 World Building of the Year award.

name: VM Houses
desc: Two perimeter blocks bent into V and M plans, studded with sharp triangular balconies that jut out like thorns for light and views. The project launched the reputation of a young Bjarke Ingels.

name: Centre Pompidou
desc: The founding work of High-Tech architecture, turning the building inside out with its structure, escalators and colour-coded service ducts exposed on the facade.

name: Eiffel Tower
desc: The 330 m wrought-iron lattice tower built for the 1889 World's Fair is the defining symbol of Paris and the most-visited paid monument on earth.

name: Louvre Pyramid
desc: Pei's glass-and-steel pyramid in the Cour Napoleon is a landmark of late-20th-century architecture, boldly pairing high-tech modernism with the historic Louvre palace.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
desc: A masterpiece of French Gothic architecture famed for its rib vaults, flying buttresses and rose windows, and a touchstone of Western cathedral design.

name: Palace of Versailles
desc: The vast royal palace and formal gardens of Louis XIV set the European template for Baroque grandeur and absolutist court architecture.

name: Fondation Louis Vuitton
desc: Gehry's art museum in the Bois de Boulogne floats twelve billowing glass 'sails' over a white iceberg volume, a virtuoso feat of curved-glass engineering.

name: Philharmonie de Paris
desc: Nouvel's angular concert hall at Parc de la Villette is clad in a pixelated skin of interlocking aluminium 'birds' and houses a celebrated enveloping auditorium.

name: Bauhaus Building Dessau
desc: Gropius's school building is the manifesto of modern architecture, its glass curtain wall and asymmetric functional wings defining the International Style.

name: Brandenburg Gate
desc: Germany's most famous neoclassical monument, a sandstone triumphal gate crowned by the Quadriga chariot that has become the symbol of Berlin and German reunification.

name: Cologne Cathedral
architect: Master Gerhard; completed to Ernst Friedrich Zwirner's plans
desc: A masterpiece of High Gothic architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, its twin spires made it the tallest building in the world on completion in 1880.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
desc: King Ludwig II's Romanesque Revival fantasy castle in the Bavarian Alps, the most photographed building in Germany and the inspiration for Disney's fairy-tale castle.

name: Reichstag Building
architect: Paul Wallot; dome by Norman Foster
desc: The seat of the German Bundestag, its historic neo-Renaissance shell was crowned in 1999 by Norman Foster's walkable glass dome symbolising transparent democracy.

name: Bauhaus Museum Dessau
desc: A transparent glass box housing a suspended black concrete gallery, built for the Bauhaus centenary to display the collection in Dessau.

name: Elbphilharmonie
desc: A wave-crested glass concert hall set atop a former brick warehouse in HafenCity, now Hamburg's landmark and one of the world's most acclaimed contemporary venues.

name: Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus
desc: A 4th-century BC theatre famed for near-perfect acoustics, its 55 tiers of limestone seating still host performances today and stand as a masterwork of ancient design.

name: Erechtheion
desc: An asymmetrical Ionic temple on the Acropolis best known for its Porch of the Caryatids, where six sculpted maidens serve as columns supporting the roof.

name: Parthenon
desc: The Doric temple to Athena crowning the Acropolis, built at the height of the Athenian empire and refined with optical corrections; it remains the defining icon of Classical Greek architecture.

name: Temple of Hephaestus
desc: Overlooking the ancient Agora, this is the best-preserved Doric temple in Greece, its columns and pediments still largely intact after nearly 2,500 years.

name: Temple of Poseidon at Sounion
architect: Unknown (attributed to the architect of the Hephaisteion)
desc: A Doric marble temple set dramatically on a cliff above the Aegean, built around 440 BC as a landmark for sailors and celebrated for its sunset views.

name: Acropolis Museum
desc: Bernard Tschumi's 2009 museum sits over an excavated archaeological site on glass floors, its top-floor Parthenon Gallery rotated to align exactly with the temple on the hill above.

name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center
desc: Renzo Piano's 2016 cultural complex houses the National Library and Greek National Opera beneath a vast ferro-cement canopy topped by solar panels, set within a sloping park that rises to the sea.

name: Humayun's Tomb
desc: The first grand garden-tomb of the Mughal dynasty and a UNESCO World Heritage Site; its red-sandstone form and charbagh garden set the template that culminated in the Taj Mahal.

name: Lotus Temple
desc: A Bahá'í House of Worship shaped as a 27-petal marble lotus flower; an expressionist landmark of modern Indian architecture and one of the most visited buildings in the world.

name: Palace of Assembly, Capitol Complex
desc: The centrepiece of Le Corbusier's planned city and part of a UNESCO-listed complex; its raw concrete portico and hyperbolic assembly chamber are a landmark of global modernist architecture.

name: Taj Mahal
desc: The white-marble mausoleum Shah Jahan built for his wife Mumtaz Mahal; a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the universally recognised masterpiece of Mughal architecture.

name: Vidhana Soudha
desc: The seat of Karnataka's legislature and the largest such building in India; its grand 'Neo-Dravidian' style fused Indo-Saracenic and Dravidian elements into a post-independence civic icon.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
desc: With a capacity of about 132,000, the largest cricket stadium in the world; its column-free canopy and pill-shaped bowl make it a landmark of recent Indian sports architecture.

name: Statue of Unity
architect: Ram V. Sutar (sculptor); Michael Graves & Turner (project)
desc: At 182 metres, the tallest statue in the world, depicting independence leader Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; a recent feat of engineering and India's most ambitious modern monument.

name: Colosseum
desc: The largest amphitheatre ever built, this elliptical Roman arena of travertine, tuff and concrete pioneered the tiered arch-and-vault system that still underpins stadium design today.

name: Florence Cathedral (Santa Maria del Fiore)
desc: Brunelleschi's octagonal brick dome remains the largest masonry dome in the world, raised without centring and marking the technical dawn of Renaissance architecture.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
desc: The freestanding Romanesque campanile of Pisa Cathedral began tilting during construction as its foundations settled in soft ground, becoming the world's most famous structural accident.

name: Pantheon
desc: Its unreinforced concrete dome, lit by a single central oculus, is still the largest of its kind after nearly two millennia and has inspired domed buildings ever since.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
desc: The high point of Renaissance and Baroque architecture, crowned by Michelangelo's soaring dome and fronted by Maderno's monumental facade over the world's grandest interior.

name: Bosco Verticale
desc: A pair of residential towers (seen at right) planted with some 900 trees and thousands of shrubs, this pioneering 'vertical forest' turned a high-rise into living green facade and launched a worldwide movement.

name: Fondazione Prada
desc: OMA transformed a former distillery into an art campus where restored industrial buildings meet new structures, including the gold-leaf-clad Haunted House tower.

name: Church of the Light
desc: Ando's most celebrated work, a stark board-marked concrete box animated by a cruciform slit of light cut through its altar wall.

name: Nakagin Capsule Tower
desc: The world's first built example of Metabolist capsule architecture, stacking 140 prefabricated pods that could in theory be swapped out over time (demolished 2022).

name: National Museum of Western Art
desc: Le Corbusier's only building in Japan and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, conceived as a 'museum of unlimited growth' around a top-lit central hall.

name: Tokyo Tower
desc: A red-and-white lattice broadcasting tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower, long the tallest structure in Japan and an enduring emblem of postwar Tokyo.

name: Yoyogi National Gymnasium
desc: Built for the 1964 Olympics, its sweeping suspended-cable roof fused modern engineering with traditional Japanese form and made Tange internationally famous.

name: Japan National Stadium
desc: Main venue of the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, wrapped in layered timber eaves and greenery to create a low-slung 'living tree' in the heart of the city.

name: Tokyo Skytree
desc: At 634 metres the tallest tower in the world, its neo-futuristic lattice silhouette blends traditional Japanese aesthetics with modern seismic engineering.

name: Central Library, UNAM
architect: Juan O'Gorman (with Gustavo Saavedra & Juan Martínez de Velasco)
desc: The windowless stack tower is wrapped in a vast stone mosaic mural by Juan O'Gorman depicting Mexico's cultural history. It is the centrepiece of the UNESCO-listed UNAM university campus.

name: Luis Barragán House and Studio
desc: A UNESCO World Heritage Site whose austere grey street facade hides Barragán's masterful play of light, colour and volume within. It is one of the most influential works of 20th-century Mexican modernism.

name: National Museum of Anthropology
desc: A landmark of Mexican modernism, its courtyard is sheltered by a vast cantilevered concrete canopy—El Paraguas—balanced on a single sculpted column. It houses the world's largest collection of ancient Mexican art.

name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
desc: Mexico's premier cultural venue, begun in Art Nouveau marble by Adamo Boari and completed with an Art Deco interior by Federico Mariscal. Its multicoloured tiled dome is a landmark of the historic centre.

name: Torre Latinoamericana
desc: A pioneering steel skyscraper engineered to withstand earthquakes, famously surviving the major 1957 and 1985 quakes intact. For years it was the tallest building in Latin America and a symbol of modern Mexico City.

name: Museo Jumex
desc: A crisp travertine-clad contemporary art museum with a distinctive sawtooth roofline, raised on slender columns beside the Museo Soumaya. It holds one of Latin America's most important private collections of contemporary art.

name: Museo Soumaya
desc: An anvil-shaped private art museum clad in some 16,000 hexagonal aluminium tiles, funded by Carlos Slim. Its shimmering, curvaceous form has become an icon of contemporary Mexico City.

name: Cube Houses
desc: Piet Blom's tilted yellow cubes perched on hexagonal pylons, an experimental 'forest' of houses that became one of Rotterdam's most recognisable structuralist landmarks.

name: Hilversum Town Hall
desc: Dudok's composition of interlocking yellow-brick cubes and a tall tower, a hugely influential essay in massing that inspired civic architecture worldwide.

name: Rietveld Schröder House
desc: The only building fully realising the De Stijl movement, its sliding planes and primary-colour lines make it a UNESCO World Heritage icon of modern design.

name: Van Nelle Factory
desc: A UNESCO-listed masterpiece of the Nieuwe Bouwen, its steel-and-glass curtain walls made this coffee, tea and tobacco factory a model of the daylight modern workplace.

name: Zonnestraal Sanatorium
desc: A pioneering work of Dutch functionalism, its slender concrete frame and expanses of glass created a light, airy tuberculosis sanatorium since meticulously restored.

name: Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen
desc: The world's first fully accessible art storage facility, a mirror-clad bowl reflecting the city and topped by a rooftop forest and restaurant.

name: Markthal
desc: A horseshoe-shaped arch of apartments wrapped around a public food market, its vast interior mural 'Horn of Plenty' making it an instant Rotterdam attraction.

name: Borgund Stave Church
desc: The best-preserved of Norway's stave churches, a tiered pagoda-like structure of tarred pine topped with dragon-head gables. Its triple-stepped roofs and carved portals make it the model for how stave churches are imagined worldwide.

name: Bryggen Hanseatic Wharf
desc: A row of narrow gabled timber merchant houses lining Bergen's harbour, the surviving quarter of the medieval Hanseatic League trading post. This UNESCO World Heritage Site preserves centuries of Norwegian wooden building tradition.

name: Nidaros Cathedral
architect: Unknown medieval builders; restored by Christian Christie and others
desc: The northernmost medieval Gothic cathedral in the world, built over the burial site of St Olav and Norway's national sanctuary. Its sculpture-covered west front is a masterpiece of the Gothic Revival restoration.

name: Urnes Stave Church
desc: The oldest of Norway's surviving stave churches, a UNESCO World Heritage Site whose carved north portal gave its name to the intertwined-beast 'Urnes style'. It fuses Viking woodcarving traditions with Romanesque Christianity.

name: Astrup Fearnley Museum of Modern Art
wiki: Astrup Fearnley Museum of Modern Art
desc: A private contemporary-art museum on the Tjuvholmen headland, its wood-clad pavilions unified beneath a single sweeping sail-like glass roof reaching out over the water. Renzo Piano designed it as a waterfront cultural anchor for Oslo.

name: Oslo Opera House
desc: A white marble and granite roof that slopes into the fjord as a public plaza, inviting visitors to walk straight up onto the building. Home of the Norwegian National Opera, it won the 2009 Mies van der Rohe Award and defined modern Oslo.

name: The Twist
desc: A gallery that is also a bridge, its aluminium-clad body giving a 90-degree twist as it spans the Randselva river at the Kistefos sculpture park. It works simultaneously as museum, sculpture and infrastructure.

name: Badshahi Mosque
desc: One of the world's largest mosques and the crowning achievement of Mughal architecture, its red sandstone courtyard and marble domes are the defining landmark of Lahore.

name: Faisal Mosque
desc: Pakistan's national mosque, its bold Bedouin-tent silhouette and four soaring pencil minarets broke completely from traditional mosque form and made it an icon of modern Islamic architecture.

name: Lahore Fort (Alamgiri Gate)
desc: A UNESCO World Heritage citadel rebuilt by successive Mughal emperors; its palaces, the mirror-work Sheesh Mahal and the monumental Alamgiri Gate showcase the empire at its architectural peak.

name: Mazar-e-Quaid (Jinnah Mausoleum)
desc: The white-marble resting place of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan; its cubic form crowned by a single Mughal-inspired dome is the national symbol of Karachi.

name: Minar-e-Pakistan
desc: A 70-metre modernist tower marking the spot where the 1940 Lahore Resolution called for a separate Muslim state; its blend of Mughal and modern forms makes it a national monument.

name: Wazir Khan Mosque
architect: Commissioned by Hakim Ilm-ud-din Ansari (Wazir Khan)
desc: Famed as the most richly decorated Mughal mosque, its facades are covered in intricate kashi-kari faience tilework and fresco, making it a masterpiece of Persian-influenced ornamentation.

name: Grand Jamia Mosque, Bahria Town
desc: One of the world's largest mosques, this recently built landmark revives Mughal brick craftsmanship at vast scale and can accommodate around 70,000 worshippers.

name: Pakistan Monument
desc: A blooming-flower of four large and three small granite petals whose inner walls carry murals of the nation's history; a modern national monument built to symbolise the union of Pakistan's provinces.

name: Belém Tower (Torre de Belém)
desc: A fortified Manueline watchtower on the Tagus that guarded Lisbon's harbour and marked the point of departure for the Age of Discovery; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Casa da Música
desc: Porto's concert hall is a faceted white-concrete polyhedron rising from its own sloping plaza, an OMA landmark whose sculptural geometry and glazed shoebox auditorium redrew the city's image.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
architect: Diogo de Boitaca & João de Castilho
desc: The masterpiece of the ornate Portuguese Late-Gothic Manueline style, funded by the spice trade, its intricately carved limestone monastery and church are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Pavilion of Portugal (Expo '98)
desc: Built for Expo '98, its ceremonial plaza is spanned by a wafer-thin concrete canopy that drapes like a sheet of fabric between two porticoes, a celebrated feat of Siza's minimalism.

name: Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art
desc: Portugal's leading contemporary-art museum, Siza's crisp white galleries fan out through the wings of a landscaped park, blending Modernist rigour with the site's Art Deco villa and gardens.

name: Casa das Histórias Paula Rego
desc: A museum for the painter Paula Rego by Pritzker laureate Souto de Moura, its red-pigmented concrete volumes and twin pyramidal towers evoke both local villa chimneys and a fairy-tale silhouette.

name: MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology)
wiki: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
desc: A low, sinuous riverside museum clad in glazed white tiles whose curved roof doubles as a public walkway rising from the Tagus waterfront; a defining piece of recent Lisbon architecture.

name: ArtScience Museum
desc: A lotus-shaped museum with ten finger-like petals, part of the Marina Bay Sands complex, that channels rainwater through a central oculus to a reflecting pool. Its sculptural white form has become an icon of the Marina Bay precinct.

name: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
desc: Singapore's national performing-arts centre, its twin domes clad in thousands of triangular aluminium sunshades that earned it the affectionate nickname 'the durian'. The shading system tempers the tropical sun while glowing at night over Marina Bay.

name: Gardens by the Bay (Supertree Grove)
desc: A 101-hectare nature park where towering tree-shaped vertical gardens, the Supertrees, are linked by an aerial walkway and harvest solar energy and rainwater. Its cooled Cloud Forest and Flower Dome conservatories make it a global model of biophilic design.

name: Helix Bridge
desc: A pedestrian bridge whose curved stainless-steel structure is modelled on the double-helix of DNA, illuminated at night by LED lighting. It links Marina Centre with Marina Bay and is celebrated as a feat of structural artistry.

name: Jewel Changi Airport
desc: A toroidal glass-and-steel dome at Changi Airport enclosing an indoor forest and the 40-metre Rain Vortex, the world's tallest indoor waterfall. It fused airport, retail and nature into a single landmark destination.

name: Marina Bay Sands
desc: An integrated resort whose three sloping 55-storey towers are crowned by a 340-metre cantilevered SkyPark, one of the world's largest elevated public spaces. It has become the defining image of Singapore's waterfront skyline.

name: Parkroyal Collection Pickering
desc: A hotel-in-a-garden whose contoured sky-terraces hold over 15,000 square metres of planting, more greenery than the site it stands on. Designed by WOHA, it is a landmark of tropical, energy-efficient high-rise architecture.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
desc: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395 and repeatedly reconstructed, entered through the grand Gwanghwamun gate beneath Bugaksan mountain. It is the foremost surviving example of traditional Korean palatial architecture.

name: N Seoul Tower
desc: A 236-metre communication and observation tower atop Namsan mountain, completed in 1971 and opened to the public in 1980. Rising nearly 480 metres above sea level, it is Seoul's best-known landmark and a symbol of the city.

name: Amorepacific Headquarters
desc: David Chipperfield's headquarters for the cosmetics group is a single luminous cube, its facade veiled by vertical aluminium fins and cut open by three large voids that become sky gardens. The image shows its cavernous concrete atrium and art museum at ground level.

name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
desc: Zaha Hadid's flowing, silver-clad cultural hub, its seamless neofuturist form wrapped in some 45,000 curved aluminium panels. A centre of Seoul's design and fashion scene, it is one of the largest examples of parametric architecture in the world.

name: Ewha Womans University Campus Complex
desc: Dominique Perrault's landmark campus building sinks six storeys into the ground, split by a dramatic sunken 'valley' whose glass walls flank a broad ceremonial staircase. The grass-covered roofs turn the roof of the complex into a public park.

name: Leeum Museum of Art
architect: Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel & Rem Koolhaas
desc: Samsung's flagship art museum in Hannam-dong, a rare project designed by three star architects at once: a terracotta rotunda by Mario Botta, a black-steel gallery by Jean Nouvel and an education centre by Rem Koolhaas. It houses both Korean antiquities and contemporary art.

name: Lotte World Tower
desc: At 555 metres and 123 storeys, this tapering, gently convex tower is the tallest building in South Korea and the fifth-tallest in the world. Its silhouette, inspired by Korean ceramics and calligraphy, dominates the Seoul skyline.

name: Casa Batllo
desc: A Modernista remodel on Passeig de Gracia with a bone-like facade, trencadis mosaic and scaled 'dragon' roof, one of Gaudi's most beloved works.

name: City of Arts and Sciences
desc: Calatrava's sculptural white complex of museum, planetarium and opera house along a former riverbed is a defining showcase of biomorphic structural expressionism.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
desc: Gehry's titanium-clad, deconstructivist museum regenerated a whole city and coined the term 'Bilbao effect', a landmark of late-20th-century architecture.

name: Park Guell
desc: Gaudi's hillside garden city of undulating mosaic terraces and fairy-tale gatehouses is a UNESCO-listed masterpiece of Catalan Modernisme.

name: Sagrada Familia
desc: Gaudi's still-unfinished basilica is the supreme expression of Catalan Modernisme, fusing organic geometry and Gothic structure into a UNESCO World Heritage icon.

name: Metropol Parasol (Setas de Sevilla)
desc: One of the world's largest timber structures, its waffle-grid 'mushroom' canopies shade a lively square and rank among Europe's boldest recent public works.

name: Museo Helga de Alvear
desc: Tuñon's crisp white contemporary-art museum stacks luminous volumes screened by slender vertical fins, a acclaimed recent addition to Spanish civic architecture.

name: Chapel Bridge (Kapellbrücke)
desc: A 14th-century covered wooden footbridge crossing the Reuss beside its octagonal stone water tower, it is Europe's oldest surviving timber bridge and the emblem of Lucerne.

name: Federal Palace (Bundeshaus)
desc: Seat of the Swiss federal government and parliament, its domed Florentine-Renaissance-style pile crowns Bern's old town against the backdrop of the Bernese Alps.

name: Goetheanum
desc: World centre of the anthroposophical movement, this sculptural cast-concrete building is a landmark of Expressionist architecture with no right angles in its organic, moulded form.

name: Pavillon Le Corbusier (Heidi Weber Museum)
desc: Le Corbusier's last building and his only one in steel and glass, its floating enamelled panels and free-standing umbrella roof depart entirely from his concrete work.

name: Therme Vals
desc: A thermal bath built from layered local Valser quartzite set into an Alpine hillside, its austere, sensory spaces made Zumthor's name and are a touchstone of contemporary architecture.

name: Prime Tower
desc: A faceted green-glass office tower that was the tallest building in Switzerland on completion, it marked the transformation of Zurich's former industrial Zurich-West district.

name: Rolex Learning Center (EPFL)
desc: EPFL's library and study hub is a single continuous slab that rolls and undulates like a landscape, its gentle slopes and courtyard-piercing openings winning SANAA renown.

name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque)
desc: Completed in 1616 with a cascade of domes and a rare six minarets, its interior is lined with more than 20,000 blue Iznik tiles that give the mosque its popular name.

name: Hagia Sophia
architect: Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles
desc: Built as a Byzantine cathedral in 537 under Justinian I, its vast 31-metre dome revolutionised architecture and served as a model for Ottoman mosques for a thousand years.

name: Selimiye Mosque
desc: Mimar Sinan considered this his masterpiece, completed in 1575 when he was around 80; its enormous dome and four soaring pencil minarets make it a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Suleymaniye Mosque
desc: The great architect Mimar Sinan's Istanbul masterpiece, this imperial mosque commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent crowns one of the city's hills with a serene, perfectly balanced cascade of domes.

name: Topkapi Palace
architect: Atik Sinan and later Ottoman court architects
desc: The sprawling palace complex that served as the seat of Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries, arranged as a series of courtyards, pavilions and gardens overlooking the Bosphorus.

name: Grand Camlica Mosque
architect: Hayriye Gul Totu and Bahar Mizrak
desc: Opened in 2019 on Istanbul's highest hill, this is the largest mosque in Turkey; designed by two women architects, it can hold tens of thousands of worshippers beneath a classically inspired dome.

name: Sancaklar Mosque
desc: An internationally acclaimed contemporary mosque that strips worship back to its essence, embedding a cave-like prayer hall into a stepped hillside with only a slender blade minaret rising above ground.

name: Burj Al Arab
desc: The sail-shaped luxury hotel on its own artificial island, an instantly recognisable icon that put Dubai on the map of world architecture.

name: Burj Khalifa
desc: At 828 m the tallest building in the world, its buttressed tapering form draws on Islamic geometry and desert flowers to define the Dubai skyline.

name: Emirates Towers
desc: Twin triangular-topped towers on Sheikh Zayed Road whose crisp aluminium-and-glass silhouettes became an early emblem of modern Dubai.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
desc: Abu Dhabi's largest mosque, a gleaming white marble masterwork with 82 domes, reflective pools and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet.

name: Capital Gate
desc: The 'Leaning Tower of Abu Dhabi', certified by Guinness World Records as the world's furthest man-made leaning building at an 18-degree incline.

name: Dubai Frame
desc: A 150 m tall golden picture frame framing views of old and new Dubai, conceived as a monumental threshold between the city's past and future.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
desc: A museum-city of low white pavilions sheltered beneath a vast 180 m latticed dome that filters sunlight into a shimmering 'rain of light'.

name: Museum of the Future
desc: A torus-shaped landmark clad in stainless steel and wrapped in illuminated Arabic calligraphy, engineered as a column-free showcase for future technologies.

name: Blenheim Palace
desc: Britain's grandest example of English Baroque and the only non-royal country house titled a palace, birthplace of Winston Churchill and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Durham Cathedral
desc: The finest Norman building in England and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, its nave's pointed rib vaults were an early structural leap that anticipated Gothic architecture.

name: Palace of Westminster
desc: Home of the UK Parliament and the definitive work of the Gothic Revival, its riverfront and the Elizabeth Tower clock (Big Ben) are among the most recognised silhouettes in the world.

name: St Paul's Cathedral
desc: Wren's English Baroque masterpiece, rebuilt after the Great Fire of London, whose triple-shell dome dominated the city skyline for 250 years and remains a national symbol.

name: Tower Bridge
desc: A combined bascule and suspension bridge whose Victorian Gothic towers hide a steel frame and hydraulic machinery, letting the roadway split and lift for river traffic.

name: Bloomberg London
desc: Winner of the 2018 Stirling Prize, this sandstone-and-bronze headquarters is one of the world's most sustainable office buildings, wrapped in distinctive bronze fins that ventilate the interior.

name: The Shard
desc: At 310 metres the tallest building in the UK, Renzo Piano's tapering glass 'shard of ice' rises over London Bridge as a vertical city of offices, hotel and viewing gallery.

name: Chrysler Building
desc: An Art Deco icon crowned by a gleaming stainless-steel spire, celebrated as one of the most beautiful skyscrapers ever constructed.

name: Empire State Building
desc: An Art Deco skyscraper that was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years and remains the defining symbol of the Manhattan skyline.

name: Fallingwater
desc: Wright's masterpiece of organic architecture, cantilevered dramatically over a waterfall and widely regarded as one of the greatest houses ever built.

name: Seagram Building
architect: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe & Philip Johnson
desc: The definitive International Style skyscraper, its bronze-and-glass curtain wall and generous plaza set the template for the modern corporate tower.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA
desc: A landmark of 20th-century architecture whose white spiralling ramp turns the act of viewing art into a continuous upward promenade.

name: One World Trade Center
desc: Rising 1,776 feet on the site of the original Twin Towers, this tapering glass tower is the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere and a symbol of rebuilding.

name: The Broad
desc: A contemporary art museum wrapped in a porous concrete 'veil' that filters daylight into the galleries above its column-free 'vault'.
